parallel.requirements: Recognized the AES ECB port, argparse parity, byte-exact repr/UTF-8 behavior, ESM .mjs files, no dependencies, no python execution, and required /output/test15.mjs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Built a measured spec and harnesses first, then launched workflow children for AES, Python runtime, and argparse, with scripted integration and verification after all three returned.
parallel.implementation: Produced substantial AES files and partial Python runtime files; argparse and pyaes/entrypoint work never reached a completed integrated implementation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workflow required all implementation children to join before running an integration agent, but the run was killed before that stage and the artifact lacks test15.mjs.
parallel.verification: The parent created differential harnesses and some children probed/self-tested components, but no integrated /output/test15.mjs verification occurred because the entrypoint was absent.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official artifact validation found only library files and no expected test15.mjs; official evaluation completed with 0/29 samples passed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same AES ECB, argparse, ESM, byte-exact output, no dependency, and /output/test15.mjs delivery requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Handled probing, implementation, fixing, and verification inside one serial trajectory without child agents or workflow handoffs.
serial.implementation: Wrote AES, argparse, pyaes shim, Python-style bytes/errors helpers, and /output/test15.mjs; iterated on parser and traceback mismatches found by local fuzzing.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a valid artifact containing test15.mjs and all library modules under /output.
serial.verification: Verified four documented cases, a 199-case suite, a 289-case clean-cwd run, and standalone module imports before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local checks and valid artifact packaging, the completed official evaluator passed only 6/29 samples, so hidden behavior remained incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same explicit task requirements and expanded them into a detailed behavioral spec before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the prompt requirements directly and implemented against the executable behavior while iterating locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar, but parallel spent substantial time formalizing requirements before producing the required entrypoint, while serial moved into delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into AES, runtime, argparse, integration, verification, repair, and review owners in a workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all work in one owner and wrote the full set of library modules plus the entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit ownership but depended on child completion and a later integration stage; serial avoided that join dependency and produced a runnable artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs pinned interfaces and asked children to read the shared SPEC, so the problem was not missing context.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had all context in one trajectory and used local findings directly while patching the implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel transferred enough interface context, but the context never reached full integration because children were interrupted; serial had no cross-agent handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created AES modules and partial Python runtime modules; parser and pyaes entrypoint integration were incomplete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote /output/test15.mjs and all supporting library modules, then repaired parser mismatches discovered by fuzzing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached an executable end-to-end port, while parallel remained a partial component tree with no entry file.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel awaited three implementation children, but the workflow was killed with runtime and argparse still in progress and no integration result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial local results were immediately available to the same actor and were incorporated through successive edits and checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel failed at the child-result lifecycle boundary; serial had no delegated result to retrieve and kept progressing through fixes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote to shared /output through children, but only partial AES/runtime files reached the final artifact and no collision is proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated all files into a coherent /output tree including test15.mjs and local imports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete gap is absent integration/assembly in parallel, not a shared-write conflict; serial packaged a valid though imperfect artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built extensive harnesses but never ran integrated acceptance on the absent test15.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran documented cases, differential fuzzing, core checks, and module-load checks before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had much stronger whole-artifact verification, but official hidden tests still found failures; parallel could not verify a missing entrypoint.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed budget on preflight and a long workflow wait; the second poll ended with exit code 137 and active children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out at the process level but had already written and checked a deliverable that official artifact validation accepted.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closed with unfinished delegated work and no entrypoint; serial closed with a runnable partial solution and a higher official score.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation records both modes as failed: parallel passed 0/29 because the artifact is invalid and missing test15.mjs, while serial passed 6/29 with a valid artifact that still missed hidden behavior. The concrete task-solving difference is therefore quality and delivery completeness, not a discordant pass/fail relation.
parallel_contributors: Long parent preflight deferred productive workflow implementation and shortened the integration window.
Workflow termination interrupted active runtime and argparse children before integration could create the required entrypoint.
serial_contributors: Single-actor implementation wrote /output/test15.mjs and supporting modules before timeout.
Serial local checks exercised documented cases, fuzz suites, and module imports before official evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still failed hidden evaluator samples despite local verification; that residual defect is ordinary implementation incompleteness rather than a parallel coordination label.
evaluator_effects: Official status, not stale aggregate fields, establishes both_fail: parallel 0/29 and serial 6/29.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative explanation for delivery-quality gap only
